extracted.intended_audience: Navy/DoD contracting officers, procurement planners, and acquisition professionals implementing OMB Circular A-76 (CITA program)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for Contracting Officers implementing OMB Circular A-76 via the Department of Defense Commercial/Industrial Type Activities (CITA) program, covering assessment, acquisition planning, solicitation/evaluation, and award/administration issues. Emphasizes cost-comparison methodology, roles/responsibilities, procedural safeguards, and communications with stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparison Process (Comparative Cost Analysis)
rubrics_metrics.description: An accurate determination of whether it is more economical to acquire the needed products or services from the private sector or from an existing or proposed Government commercial or industrial activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Cost Comparison Handbook (Supplement to A-76) for detailed methodology; apply incremental costing where appropriate; include all relevant direct and indirect costs, fringe benefits, overhead, and cost differentials; verify in-house estimates; document analysis to support conversion/new-start decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of the Availability of Commercial Sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether a product or service is obtainable from private/commercial sources before treating an activity as a CITA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activity must be separable and regularly needed; survey the commercial marketplace, consider commercial items and services, and confirm the existence of adequate private-sector capacity and competition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify and treat activities that comprise multiple distinct functions when applying the A-76 process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate separability of functions, potential for packaging or multiple-function contracts, and the implications on cost comparison and competition; caution against inappropriate bundling that obscures cost/comparison equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of Same Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider consolidating identical functions across organizations in the assessment/acquisition process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess economies of scale and administrative impact; consolidation may change cost comparison outcomes and require re-evaluation of milestones, staffing, and procurement methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications with Interested Groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Proactive communication with stakeholders (unions, civil service, contractors, Congress, GAO, OMB, OFPP) during A-76 implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide timely notices, public review of cost-comparison results, respond to inquiries, and ensure equitable treatment of affected parties to reduce disputes and political scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational and Staffing Issues (Acquisition Planning)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the organization and staffing required within the contracting office to execute CITA-related acquisitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure sufficient contracting personnel, assign responsibilities, clarify lines of authority, and address dichotomies between systems/field commands; plan for workload and training needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Workload Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how CITA implementation affects contracting workload and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate procurement volume, processing burden, and necessary changes to staffing or priorities; use workload impact to inform milestone and resource planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement Administrative Lead Time
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for realistic procurement administrative lead times in milestone planning and acquisition schedules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for time for solicitation development, pre-proposal conferences, evaluation, negotiations, public review, and award; adjust milestones to reflect Navy/FAR/DAR lead-time guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure proper delegation and exercise of contracting authority in support of CITA procurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify authorized officials, limits of authority, required approvals, and coordinate with higher-level commands when statutory or policy thresholds are crossed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide contracting officers and acquisition staff with training on A-76 policy, cost-comparison methodology, solicitation/evaluation techniques, and related regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize new or revised methodologies needed to conform with policy requirements; use OFPP/Navy training seminars and highlighted procurement materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Task Group
rubrics_metrics.description: Use multi-disciplinary task groups to oversee assessment, acquisition planning, and cost-comparison activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contracting, legal, technical, manpower, and financial representatives to ensure comprehensive analysis and defendable decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Milestone Planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop and adhere to milestone schedules for the CITA program cycle from assessment through conversion and administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define typical milestone development, link Phase I/II/III activities to dates, and include decision points for public review, appeals, and award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of Work (SOW)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a clear, complete, and measurable SOW for services to be procured under CITA-related contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SOW must describe required tasks/outputs, performance standards, and contract administration requirements to enable fair competition and accurate cost proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity of the System
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain fairness, equity, and integrity throughout the A-76 acquisition and cost-comparison process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conflicts of interest, ensure accurate disclosure of information, prevent practices such as wage-busting, and guard against actions that would undermine public confidence or program equity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense Acquisition Regulation / Contract Clauses (Pre-solicitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Select and apply the appropriate DAR/FAR contract clauses in solicitations supporting CITA procurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure clauses reflect service contract issues, labor standards, firm-cost concepts, and special A-76-related provisions; coordinate with legal and procurement policy offices for case-specific clause selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of Supply: Set-asides
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider set-aside programs (small business, Section 8(a), etc.) when planning solicitations for CITA procurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review small business eligibility, 8(a) procedures, and other socio-economic programs to determine appropriate procurement strategies while balancing competition and policy goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicitation Methodologies and Contract Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose solicitation methodologies and contract types suited to the service being procured under the CITA program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider firm-fixed-price, cost-reimbursement, firm-cost/firm-bid procedures where applicable; select methods that support fair evaluation, risk allocation, and cost-comparison integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options and the Cost Comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for contract options in the cost-comparison process and in preparing solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Model option periods consistent with Government requirements and potential in-house costs; ensure options do not distort the comparative economics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-bid / Pre-proposal Conferences
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences to clarify requirements and promote informed competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use conferences to explain the SOW, procurement schedule, evaluation factors, and how government in-house estimates will be handled; document discussions and disseminate minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negotiations
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct fair and effective negotiations with offerors while preserving competition and integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow negotiation best practices in accordance with FAR/DAR, document negotiation positions, and ensure consistent treatment of all offerors; avoid disclosing competitive information improperly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competition
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximize and preserve competition in CITA-related procurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure solicitations and timelines to encourage multiple offerors, avoid bundling that reduces competition, and follow competition-promoting set-aside policies where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of Low Bid / Offer
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate low bids/offers for realism and compliance with solicitation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether low bids reflect understanding of the SOW, proper labor/payroll levels, fringe benefits, and applicable wage determinations; adjust or reject unrealistic offers per procurement regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation / Award Factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and apply evaluation and award factors appropriate to service procurements under A-76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include technical capability, past performance, cost/price, responsibility, and any specialized criteria; ensure factors are balanced to achieve economy and efficiency as A-76 intends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Late Submission of Government In-house Cost Estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for handling late submissions of the Government in-house cost estimate during the solicitation/evaluation cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish deadlines, describe consequences of late submissions, and provide equitable treatment to offerors; late in-house estimates can affect fairness and public review schedules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revealing the Government In-house Cost Estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on if, when, and how the government in-house cost estimate is disclosed to offerors or the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance transparency/public review with protecting procurement integrity; follow A-76/public review rules about announcement of results and appropriate timing for revealing estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement of the Results of the Cost Comparison / Public Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Make public the results of cost comparisons and provide opportunity for review and comment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish results, permit public inspection/comment per Circular procedures, and document responses; public review is intended to ensure equitable treatment and transparency for affected parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of the Government In-house Cost Estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify the accuracy and completeness of the Government in-house cost estimate used in comparisons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent checks, reconcile accounting bases, confirm fringe benefit rates, and ensure estimates reflect operations as proposed; verification is essential to withstand challenges and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals versus Protests
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate and handle appeals (internal administrative) and protests (GAO or other forum) arising from cost-comparison decisions and awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform stakeholders of appeal rights, follow prescribed appeal procedures, anticipate potential GAO protests, and prepare documentation to defend decisions and mitigate litigation risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: CITA and CITASS Definitions and Scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and scope rules for Commercial or Industrial Type Activity (CITA) and its support services (CITASS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A CITA must be separable and regularly needed; CITASS are services resulting from operation of a CITA; distinguish CITASS from other contractor support services (CSS) and exclude certain R&D/GOCO/GOGO cases per policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Function (Exception Criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria identifying functions that must be performed by Government personnel (in-house) due to special governmental responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government functions include discretionary application of Government authority, monetary transactions/entitlements, and maintenance of in-house technical core capabilities; such functions are excluded from conversion to contract performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion, New Start, and Expansion Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions and thresholds governing conversion of work to contract, establishing new in-house activities (new starts), and expansions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion = transfer of work to contractor; New Start includes newly established Government C/I activities and certain expansions; Expansion thresholds defined by capital investment ($100k) or annual operating cost increases ($200k) and percentage criteria for treatment under A-76.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Differentials (Thresholds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost margins established by A-76 that must be exceeded before initiating a new start in-house or before converting in-house activity to contract performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply specified differentials to ensure marginal differences do not drive unwarranted conversions or starts; use these thresholds in comparative analyses and decision documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Incremental Costing and Treatment of Employee Benefit Rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Methodology for calculating in-house costs, including incremental costing and proper accounting for insurance, retirement, and other fringe benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use incremental costing where appropriate per transmittal memoranda; be aware that changes in fringe benefit rate assumptions (e.g., 10.7% to 28.7% then 18.1%) materially affect cost comparisons and must be transparently applied and documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm Cost Concept (DAR Case 76-144 and 'firm bid/offer' usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of the 'firm cost' or firm bid/offer procedures in procurements supporting the C/I program to ensure reliable pricing for cost comparisons and award stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow NAVSUP/NAVMAT guidance and DAR/FAR guidance for using firm-bid/offer procedures; coordinate incorporation of firm-cost concepts into solicitations when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing 'Wage Busting' for Professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures to ensure contractor proposals for professional services do not undercut required wages or labor standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow OFPP Letter No. 78-2 and related guidance for evaluating contractor proposals to prevent suppression of professional wages and ensure compliance with Service Contract Act and other labor protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Section 8(a) and Small Business Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Consideration of socio-economic procurement programs (e.g., Section 8(a)) when implementing CITA procurements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess use of 8(a) and other small business procedures consistent with Navy and OFPP guidance, balancing policy goals and competition requirements.
